name: 1 · TUNE ONE EDGE  ─  line-finder is the setup tool, not the cropper
info:
`line-finder` never crops anything. It measures ONE straight edge inside
ONE region you draw, so you can get that edge solid before handing the
numbers to `label-crop` (section 2), which runs four of them itself.

Open the `line finder` node, load a sample frame into its canvas and
drag across the edge you want - the drag *direction* sets the scan
direction. Then hit Inject and read the preview drawn on the canvas:

  blue parallelogram = the search region
  green ticks        = calipers that agreed and were used in the fit
  red ticks          = calipers dropped as outliers
  yellow line        = the fitted line

Tune until it is found on every frame you try, with few red ticks:

  * found nothing        -> lower `contrastThreshold`; if only some
                            calipers find it, lower
                            `minCaliperFraction` too
  * found the WRONG edge -> tighten the region, do NOT raise contrast
  * soft, multi-step     -> `Edge select` = `first` or `last` instead
    transition              of `best`. `best` picks the strongest step,
                            which flips between two similar ones from
                            frame to frame; `first`/`last` are
                            positional, so they stay on the same step.
                            This is what makes a boundary repeatable.
  * a few red ticks      -> widen the region so the edge stays inside it
                            on every frame, or raise
                            `outlierTolerancePx` a little

The region loaded here is this rig's *top* edge - the hardest one, a
4-grey-level step that is never found at the default contrast of 2.
Repeat for the other three, then move to section 2.

name: 2 · CROP  ─  label-crop in calipers mode runs four line finders itself
info:
`label-crop` with **Boundary = calipers** runs no blob search at all. It
greys the frame once, runs one line finder per side over the regions in
the `edgeRegions` JSON, intersects the four fitted lines into a
rectangle, then deskews and crops to it - the same rotate/crop tail the
blob mode uses.

The scan direction per side is implied (left scans rightwards, top
scans downwards, ...), so each side needs only its box plus whichever
line-finder options you tuned in section 1. Every option in
`lib/lineFinder.js` is accepted per side.

Coordinates are FULL-RESOLUTION frame pixels. Calipers mode ignores
`maxEdge` and measures at full res on purpose - a caliper looks for a
position, not a shape, so a 640px detection copy would coarsen every
reading 6x.

If one edge is not found the frame is NOT cropped:
`msg.labelCrop.reason` names the side (e.g.
`calipers:missing-edge:top`) and `msg.labelCrop.edges` carries per-side
diagnostics (found / reason / score / calipers / residualPx) so you can
see which region to re-aim. Guessing a missing edge would silently
mis-crop, so it refuses instead.

Measured with the regions below over this rig's 148 good frames:

  found on           148/148
  label width spread 1.8 px
  height spread      5.2 px
  deskew angle spread 0.14 deg

and of the 14 bad frames it refuses 6 outright - the blanks, which have
no label boundary to find.

Note the lowered `minCaliperFraction`. Left, right and top are found
by all 16 calipers on every one of the 148 frames, but the bottom edge
is picked up by only a third of them - 5 of 16 at worst - so at the 0.5
default it is reported missing on 76 of them. Lowering the fraction is
the right fix there, not raising contrast.

name: 3 · WHAT NOT TO EXPECT from cropping (measured on this rig)
info:
The crop above is geometrically excellent and still does not improve
the inspection on this label. Measured over 148 good / 14 bad frames
against a Demo_Good_60 golden:

  no crop           148/148 good pass
  blob crop          72/148
  fixed rect         55/148
  calipers crop      28/148

The cause is not the crop quality. The recurring background-defect
regions sit on logotype strokes and barcode bar fields - real fine
artwork in the label's left margin. Cropping shifts
which pixels land in which comparison block, which moves that artwork
relative to the golden and makes the mismatch worse.

So use this flow when you want a deskewed, consistently framed label
image - archiving, OCR, a downstream tool that wants the label alone -
not as a way to raise the inspection score. See ARCHITECTURE.md,
"What it does not solve".
